And he again sets faith and drawing back in opposition the one to the other, and also the preservation of the soul to its perdition.
Now let it be noticed that this truth belongs also to us, for we, whom God has favored with the light of the Gospel, ought to acknowledge that we have been called in order that we may advance more and more in our obedience to God, and strive constantly to draw nearer to him. This is the real preservation of the soul, for by so doing we shall escape eternal perdition.
CHAPTER 11
Hebrews Chapter 11:1
1. Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.
1. Porro fides est rerum sperandarum substantia, demonstratio eorum quae non videntur.

               <ns0:head>CHAP. X.</ns0:head>
               <ns0:p n="1">1 FOR <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">This <ns0:hi>For</ns0:hi> is connecting this to the fore-going Discourse, and is a further Improvement of the Argument laid down, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 9. proving the Necessity and Excellency of the one Sacri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fice offered by Christ for Sinners unto God, from the weak<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness of all the legal ones. For if all the multitude of them were not able to take away Sins, and Christ's one Offering is mighty to abolish them, and to perfect all who use it, then not these legal ones, but his is necessary to be valued by the <ns0:hi>Hebrews,</ns0:hi> and preferred to that end; the Demonstration of which takes up from <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 1, to 19. of this Chapter.</ns0:note> the law <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>The whole Mosaical Oeconomy</ns0:hi> given from God to <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> by him in the Wilderness of <ns0:hi>Sina</ns0:hi>; Priesthood, Covenant, Sacrifices and Services, which that did contain.</ns0:note> having a shadow <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Chap. 8.5. <ns0:hi>A shadow</ns0:hi> is lower than an <ns0:hi>Image,</ns0:hi> and of another kind from the re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ality or Substance; a dark, obscure representation of what was to fulfil them, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> of Christ, with all his Ministry and Priviledges attending his Covenant, both for Time and E<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ternity; this the Mosaical Law-real comprehended, but all in <ns0:hi>Shadow-work.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> of good things to come, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> not the very image <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">They are not the very Essence and Sub<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stance themselves of those things, the Pattern, or real Sam<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plar, but a shadowy Representation; they lead their Users to Christ and his matters, which they represented, but were not the substantial good things themselves. So <ns0:hi>Image</ns0:hi> is read, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 15.49. we have carried the <ns0:hi>Image</ns0:hi> of the earthly <ns0:hi>A<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dam,</ns0:hi> that is, his Nature,</ns0:note> of the things, can never with those sacri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fices which they offered year by year continu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ally, make <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>legal Sacrifices</ns0:hi> are not only <ns0:hi>impotent</ns0:hi> in respect of their Constitution, but of their very Nature, being only Shadows, so as they cannot render a Soul compleat, either in respect of Justification or Sanctification, it could not free any either from the Guilt or Punishment of Sin at present, much less eternally, with all the Renovation of them either on the Day of Atonement yearly, or those daily offered by them, tho they should continue to be offered for ever, yet could they not perfect either the Priests mi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nistring, or those for whom they ministred, who were ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ternally humbling themselves on the Expiation-day. They being designed only to point the People to this better Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crifice of Christ, which was to perfect them, that Work be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing so noble, and above the power of Shadows to per<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />form.</ns0:note> the commers thereunto perfect:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:561" />2 For then <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>They would have cea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sed to be offered, because,</ns0:hi> &c.</ns0:note> would they not have ceased to be offered <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>For,</ns0:hi> proves the weakness of that shadowy Service un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der the Law, because it never ceased, which it would if it had perfected its Users; and having reached its end, and done that Work, have ceased; for these Sacrifices would not of right have been repeated, neither needed they, if they could have justified and sanctified Souls for ever.</ns0:note>, because that the worshippers once purged <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">For then this effect would have followed, the Worshippers who were to be atoned for, or expiated by these Sacrifices, if they had perfected them, <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> pardoned, justified and ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quitted them from Guilt of Sin and Punishment, there would have nothing remained to have troubled, vexed, or tormented their Souls, they being no further accused or con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />demned by their Conscience about Sin, God having justified and sanctified them, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 9.14, 26, 28. comp. <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 5.1, 2, 11.</ns0:note>, should have had no more conscience of sins:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 But <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">If the legal Sacrifices could have perfected their Offerers, there would have been no Remembrance of Sins; <ns0:hi>but</ns0:hi> there is a Remembrance of Sins yearly, therefore they are weak and cannot perfect.</ns0:note> in <ns0:hi>those sacrifices there is</ns0:hi> a <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">These shadowy Sacrifices yearly re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />iterated, still left Sins in their Guilt and killing Power, load<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing and grinding the Conscience by Accusation and Con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />demnation for them, as well as setting them in the Light of God's Countenance. For in the Expiation-day <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi> was <ns0:hi>to remember and to confess</ns0:hi> over the Head of the Scape-Goat, laying his hands on it, all the Churches Sins of the past Year and Life, notwithstanding former Expiatory-Sacrifices offered for them, <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 16.22. For as soon as that was done, their expiating Virtue vanished, and so they renewed Sacrifices without any spiritual Profit by them, the Guilt of past and present Sins remaining still: whereas Christians now renewing Sin, do renew their Faith and Repentance, but not their Sacrifice for it; the Virtue of which in a full and fi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nal Absolution applied to them by the Spirit, makes them to have, upon their final Accounts, no Conscience of Sin for ever.</ns0:note> remem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />brance again <ns0:hi>made</ns0:hi> of sins every year.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4 For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 9.13.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>For,</ns0:hi> gives a reason of the precedent Proof, That the <ns0:hi>le<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gal Sacrifices did keep Sins in Remembrance; for</ns0:hi> they were of such matter as could not have any causal Power to take them away.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:hi>it is</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">This is equivalent to an Universal Negative, the <ns0:hi>Impossibility</ns0:hi> being absolute as to the things themselves in their very Nature, they being corporeal, can have no Influ<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ence upon a spiritual Evil in the Soul, <ns0:hi>Mich.</ns0:hi> 6.6, 7. and by God's Constitution they were to lead them to better things, God being not pleased with Flesh and Blood, <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> 50.13. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 1.11.</ns0:note> not possible that the blood of bulls <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">The Blood of these were only carried into the Holy of Holiest on the Atonement-day, yearly, <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 16. to which this is chiefly applied; nor could the Blood of all the other Sacrifices by Expiation, pardon their Offerers, nor by Sanctification cleanse them, nor by removing the sense of them, comfort the Soul; they could neither pacifie God, nor the Sinners Conscience, having no Virtue or Power to satisfie God's Justice, or merit his Grace, only it had by his Constitution a Power to type out <ns0:hi>that Blood</ns0:hi> which could do both.</ns0:note> and of goats, should take away sins.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 Wherefore <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">

                     </ns0:gap> introduceth the Proof of the Invalidity of legal Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crifices, and the Efficacy of the one Sacrifice of Christ, from Divine Testimony about both of them.</ns0:note> when he cometh into the world, he saith, <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">God the Son, who existed before his Incarnation, <ns0:hi>bespeaketh</ns0:hi> God the Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, when he was coming into this World, to become a part of it, by uniting an holy Human Nature to the Divine, as <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> voucheth by the Spirit of God, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 40.6.                <ns0:p n="6">6 In burnt-offerings and <ns0:hi>sacrifices</ns0:hi> for sin <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Two other sorts of Sacrifices are added to the former, as <ns0:hi>whole Burnt-offerings,</ns0:hi> which were all devoured by Fire on God's Altar, and no part of them came to the Priests, <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 1.3, 9, 10, 13, 14, 17. These four sorts of Sacrifices compre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hend all the <ns0:hi>Aaronical</ns0:hi> Offerings for Expiation: God did not require or desire any of these for themselves, or for the perfecting of Sinners: He did not as to such an end approve them, or take any pleasure in them.</ns0:note> thou hast had no pleasure:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 Then said I, <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">When the Father declared the Sacrifices of Beasts and Birds would not please him, nor be accepted for expiating Sins, <ns0:hi>then I said,</ns0:hi> I appeared in Person, and declared, <ns0:hi>Lo, I come with a fit and proper Sacrifice; I approach</ns0:hi> my self with my Human Nature, fully resolved to offer that to Thee as a Propitiatory Sacrifice, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 12.27. comp. <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> 40.7.</ns0:note> Lo, I come (in the vo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lume <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">

And in the entrance of them the Spirit testifieth of his Deity, and of his Union to the Humanity, being to be conceived and born of a Vir<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gin, and offering himself a Sacrifice to expiate Sin, and re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />concile Sinners, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 3.15. comp. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 5.46, 47.</ns0:note> of the book it is written of me) to do <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">To obey his Fathers Command, of dying an Expiatory Sacrifice for Sinners. This Will of God was in his Heart, he delighted to obey it, <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> 40.8. and his own natural Will that would regret it, he would deny, and would not use his Divine Power to deliver him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self from it, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 26.39, 46. <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 18.11.</ns0:note> thy will, O God.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 Above <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">In this Verse the Apostle repeats the whole Testimony, produced out of the <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> only with a Specification in a <ns0:hi>Pa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />renthesis; which are offered by the Law,</ns0:hi> viz. such Sacrifices, against which the Apostle argueth, which could not purge away Sin, nor procure Righteousness, nor make no more Conscience of Sins. He observes from the <ns0:hi>Psalm,</ns0:hi> that the Will of God was plainly signified by his Spirit to <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> under the Law, about the Nature, State and Design of his Institution of Sacrifices, that they were typical of, and lead<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing to a better Sacrifice than themselves; and that for their own sake only, they were no way acceptable to God, and so rejected by him.</ns0:note> when he said, Sacrifice, and of<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fering, and burnt-offerings, and <ns0:hi>offering</ns0:hi> for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure <ns0:hi>there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />in,</ns0:hi> (which are offered by the Law:)</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 Then <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">In this Verse the Apostle collects the Psalmists Asser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of God the Father's accepting his Sacrifice, the offering whereof was so exactly agreeable to his Will, when he was displeased with the legal ones, and this revealed to <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> when he was punctually using them according to the Law.</ns0:note> said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">God therefore abolished all the legal Sacrifices, which he commanded to be used as Types of the better Sacrifice he had provided, because of their Insufficiency and Weakness as to expiate Sin, or pacifie Conscience, that he might esta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />blish that Sacrifice of the Body of Christ for abolishing Sin, and bringing in everlasting Righteousness, which was effectual, and an actual Obedience agreeable to his Will and Command, <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 2.7, 8. This being thus proved, he concludes from it, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 10.</ns0:note> that he may establish the second.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 By the which <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">That spoken of, <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> 40.8. <ns0:hi>that Will</ns0:hi> and Command of God given to Christ, God-Man, that he should once offer up his Body a Sacrifice for Sin, which he willingly and heartily obeyed, <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 2.8.</ns0:note> will we are sanctified <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Sanctified</ns0:hi> is to be taken largely for a Communication to us of all the Benefits of Redemption, as Pardon, Reconciliation, Absolution from Punishment, Reno<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vation of God's Image, and such a Discharge of Sin at last, as never to be guilty of it more, Perfection of Grace in Glo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 9.12.</ns0:note> through the offering <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">The voluntary and heartily yeilding it up, and pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />senting the Blood of it to the Father within the Veil in Hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven to atone him according to his own Command and Will, without which it would not have been accepted by him, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 23.46. comp. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 20.15, 17, 18. and 19.28, 30.</ns0:note> of the body <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">It was that part of Christ's Person that was to die a Sacri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fice, and the Blood of it that was to be shed for purchasing the Remission of Sins, as appears in the Memorial of it, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 22.19, 20. The <ns0:hi>very Body o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> God-Man,</ns0:hi> Acts 20.28. The <ns0:hi>once</ns0:hi>-Offering of which was eternally available to take away Sin from Sinners, and perfect them to Glory. So that God's end being once reached in it, it is of perpetual Vir<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tue to apply its Fruits to believing Penitents, and needs not any Repetition.</ns0:note> of Jesus Christ once <ns0:hi>for all.</ns0:hi>

                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:562" />11 And <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Having proved, that not <ns0:hi>the yearly</ns0:hi> repeated Legal Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crifices could perfect a Sinner, but only the Sacrifice of Christ, the Spirit proceeds to prove, that the <ns0:hi>daily</ns0:hi> legal Sacrifi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ces can do as little for this Work as the <ns0:hi>annual</ns0:hi>; and there<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore these <ns0:hi>Hebrews</ns0:hi> ought to desert all these, and depend only upon Christ's. From <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 11, to 19. <ns0:hi>every Priest</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Aaron</ns0:hi>'s Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mily in his Course daily ministring, <ns0:hi>stood at the Altar,</ns0:hi> and performed the Service appointed him by God, <ns0:hi>offering often</ns0:hi> the same bloody Sacrifices to God, of Bulls, Goats, Sheep, Fowl, many times in one day, and for many days together, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 7.27.</ns0:note> every priest standeth daily mini<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />string, and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">These were not available either to the Priests Offering, or those who brought them to be offered for the spiritual and eternal Expiation of their Sins, as to their Guilt, Stain, Power or Punishment, not any, nor all of these, none could do it at any time. See <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 4.</ns0:note> never take away sins.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 But <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Opposed to the Legal Priests is <ns0:hi>this Priest,</ns0:hi> God-Man, an Almighty Minister, having <ns0:hi>once</ns0:hi> offered, and no more, <ns0:hi>one</ns0:hi> Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crifice of his Body for the Sins of others (he had none of his own, as every other Priest had) that they might be pardoned and remembred no more, it being of eternal Virtue and Efficacy. <ns0:hi>For ever</ns0:hi> must be joyned to the <ns0:hi>Sacrifice</ns0:hi> to com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pleat the Opposition, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 11. The legal one could <ns0:hi>never</ns0:hi> take away Sins, but his <ns0:hi>one</ns0:hi> Sacrifice could take them away <ns0:hi>for ever.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> this man after he had offered one sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />
                  <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                  </ns0:gap>ri<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                     <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>ce for sins, <ns0:hi>f</ns0:hi> for ever sate down on the right hand of God <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">He c<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ased from sacrificing any more, and ascended up to Heaven, and there he <ns0:hi>sate himself</ns0:hi> down (having abolished Sin, and finished his Work as a Servant for ever) in the highestPlace of Dominion and Power at <ns0:hi>God</ns0:hi>'s <ns0:hi>Right-hand,</ns0:hi> while the <ns0:hi>Aaro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nites stood</ns0:hi> trembling and waiting at God's Foot-stool; and thence he powerfully and efficaciously commands the blot<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ting out of Sins, applieth his Merits, and dispenseth to his Servants the Covenant-mercies which he purchased by his own Blood for them, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 1.3. and 2.9. and 8.2.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 From henceforth <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">That which remaineth he expecteth, even the fulfil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ling of his Father's Promise to him, <ns0:hi>Psalm</ns0:hi> 110.1. patiently waiting, earnestly looking for what is most certain, and wherein he cannot be disappointed; for in respect of him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self, his Enemies cannot infest him more, being entirely van<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quished already, but in respect of his Administration, he waits till all that oppose his Royal Priesthood, as the Devil and his Angels, Sin, the Curse, Death, and the World, with which he conflicts as a Priest to destroy them with his own Blood, as his Members do by it, <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 12.11. Having given them their deaths Wound by his own Death, he sits down, and waits in the successive Ages of his Church, until upon his Elect it be made good, putting all under his own and Churches Feet, so to over-come and trample on them, as Men on their Foot-stools. See <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 2.8. 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 15<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>26.</ns0:note> expecting <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 10.13.</ns0:note> till his e<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nemies be made his foot-stool.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 For by one <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>For,</ns0:hi> here gives the Reason of the precedent Effect, and it is opposed to the Reason of the legal Offerings defect; their Sacrifices multiplied could not perfect Sinners, but this <ns0:hi>one</ns0:hi> doth it fully; <ns0:hi>For by one,</ns0:hi> &c.</ns0:note> offering he hath <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Christ, God-Man, the Gospel-High-Priest by the <ns0:hi>one</ns0:hi> Offering of himself a Sacrifice for Sin to God his Father, and <ns0:hi>once</ns0:hi> performed by him, hath secured Perfection of Justification, Sanctification, and Bles<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sedness, perpetually to be continued, whereby the Persons interested in it, are qualified and consecrated to be Priests to God and his Father (as the <ns0:hi>Aaronical</ns0:hi> Priests were by the Sacrifice of the Ram of Consecration, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 29.22, 24.) to serve in their proportion here, but especially after the completion of it by their Resurrection, they shall perfectly serve him before his Throne in the Holy of Holiest for ever, 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 2.9. <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 1.6. and 5.10. and 20.6.</ns0:note> perfect<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed for ever them that are <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">The renewed Souls by the Holy Ghost, such whose Consciences he hath sprinkled with the Blood of Jesus, and by it freed them from the Guilt of Sin and its Punishment, and whose Natures he regenerates and sanctifieth, freeing them from their evil Ha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bits, and making them inherently Holiness unto the Lord, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 110.3. 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 6.11.</ns0:note> sanctified.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 <ns0:hi>Whereof</ns0:hi> the holy Ghost <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">The Assumption cleared before, the Apostle now pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceedeth to prove out of the Old Testament, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> That God's purpose was, by Christ's one Sacrifice, to take away all Sins for ever; therefore there was no need of the Repetition of the legal Sacrifices. The Authority avouched, is the Te<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stimony of the <ns0:hi>Holy Spirit of Truth,</ns0:hi> that cannot deceive, nor be deceived in what it witnesseth, but confirms the Truth be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />yond all just ground of doubting, by his <ns0:hi>A<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>anuensis</ns0:hi> the Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phet <ns0:hi>Ieremiah,</ns0:hi> ch. 31.31, 33, 34. where the Person that the Prophet stileth <ns0:hi>Iehovah,</ns0:hi> is by the Apostle declared to be the <ns0:hi>Holy Ghost</ns0:hi>; and by it is proved to be the eternal God. He testifieth <ns0:hi>to us</ns0:hi> the Church of God in the Prophets time, and to us all called to be Members of it to this day.</ns0:note> also is a wit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness to us: for after <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">This contains the Preface of the Spirit's Testimony, that which he spake before, the Covenant, which is his Evidence, and this Preface is laid down, <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 31.31. Here they are all the A<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />postle's Words.</ns0:note> that he had said be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 This <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">God promiseth his true <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> his entring with them into a new Testamental Covenant, after the days that the Co<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />venant-Administration at <ns0:hi>Sinai</ns0:hi>: was expired, then <ns0:hi>the Lord saith,</ns0:hi> Jer. 31.33. That he will renew Minds and Hearts by his Spirit, and conform them to his Will, that they shall be living, walking exemplars of his Law, of both which see <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 8.10. This work of Sanctification of Souls is properly inferred here, to prove that such as en<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />joy it are perfected by Christ, because <ns0:hi>the Promise of Holi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness is joined with that of perfect Righteousness. Formerly</ns0:hi> it was urged from the Text to another purpose, to prove God's Will of changing the <ns0:hi>Aaronical</ns0:hi> Administration of the Co<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />venant, because this was better; <ns0:hi>Here</ns0:hi> it is urged to prove the perfect effect of the Sacrifice of Christ once offered to God, without which these Promises of the Covenant of Ju<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stifying and Sanctifying Sinners had neither been made nor effected.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord: I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them;</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 And <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">God covenanteth to give no<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> only Sanctification, but Justification to his Believing <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> so as their Sins shall be remitted, and God will solemnly absolve them from the punishment they merit, see <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 8.12. promised <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 31.34. In which proof though there be no express mention of the Sacrifice of Christ, yet is it implyed, for it is urged by the Spirit to that purpose; and in other Scriptures, speaking of the same thing here promised, it is expressed, as hath been shewn <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 8.6. compare <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 53. That the Death of Christ confirms this Covenant, of which he is Me<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />diator, and secures remission of Sin for ever to the duly-qualified-subject for it.</ns0:note> their sins and iniquities will I re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />member no more.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 Now <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">The Spirit having cleared his Assumption before, <ns0:hi>now</ns0:hi> concludes; whereas perfect Forgiveness of Sins is from God's Grace by the one Sacrifice of his Son once offered, acquired and effected for penitent Believers for ever, as the Promise voucheth, <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 31.32. <ns0:hi>For he will in no wise remember their Sins, but will forgive them for ever</ns0:hi>; therefore there needs no Repetition of that Sacrifice again, or of any other for Sin. But the <ns0:hi>Hebrews</ns0:hi> had the highest reason now to desert the Le<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gal Sacrifices, and to rest upon, and to cleave to his alone, any Being, Use or Consistency of such, after the Effect of Christ's one Sacrifice, being vain: For all being compleated in his, it is but just theirs should cease from them.</ns0:note> where remission of these <ns0:hi>is, there is</ns0:hi> no more offering for sin.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 Having <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">At this Verse the Spirit applieth and maketh use of the Doctrine of the great Gospel-High-Priest, and his one All-sufficient Sacrifice, and continueth it through part of the thirteenth Chapter.                      </ns0:gap>, <ns0:hi>therefore,</ns0:hi> which refers to the whole of his doctrinal Discourse before of the Excellency of the Gospel-HighPr-iest, for his Person, as to both his Natures being God-Man, and his Sacrifice with its Effects.                <ns0:p n="21">21 And <ns0:hi>having</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 4.14, 16.</ns0:note> an high priest <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Christians have not only a <ns0:hi>Liberty</ns0:hi> of coming, but a <ns0:hi>Way</ns0:hi> wherein, and a <ns0:hi>help</ns0:hi> whereby to reach home to God; which help is a <ns0:hi>surpassing Priest</ns0:hi> to all others, the great and eminent one for real Worth and Dignity, Christ himself, God-man, exalted to the right hand of the Majesty on high, after he had fulfilled his Work here, where he was invested with all Authority and Power, and set over the Church of the living God, consisting both of <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Gentile Israelites,</ns0:hi> ch. 3.6. <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 20.28. whose Sacrifices of Praise and Prayer offered up to God, he presenteth, perfumed with the Incense of his own Merits before the Throne, representing their Persons, pleading their Cause, and continually interceeding for their Good, making all they are, and perform, acceptable to his Father by his own Blood, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 8.2.</ns0:note> over the house of God;</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 Let us <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">This contains the Duty grounded on, and encouraged to by the former Priviledges, <ns0:hi>viz,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>spiritual motion</ns0:hi> of his Church, using Christ for their coming home to God, in Prayer, and all parts of Worship and Conversation; See <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 4.16. and 7.25.</ns0:note> draw near with a true <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">With <ns0:hi>Sincerity and Integrity of Heart,</ns0:hi> both as it is the Subject of Actions, and exercising them as such in all Acts of Worship and Service unto God, when the Mind and Heart is fixed to perform all strictly, according to God's Will, for matter and manner, so as to reach him Glory, and to ob<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tain from him a Blessing, <ns0:hi>Psal</ns0:hi> 37.31.</ns0:note> heart, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Eph. 3.12.</ns0:note> in full assurance of faith <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">

                     <ns0:hi>The Body</ns0:hi> (as the Priests were under the Law washed before their Service) is <ns0:hi>the outward Man,</ns0:hi> which is as well as the Soul to the sanctified by the holy Spirit, and cleansed from all filthiness of Flesh: These cor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rupt Members of the old Man must be put off, and mortified by the Spirit of God, before they can be fit to approach to worship him, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 6.11, 19, 20. 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 7.1. <ns0:hi>Ezek.</ns0:hi> 36.25. 1 <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 3.3.</ns0:note> bodies washed with pure water.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 Let us <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">This Duty is inferred from the Doctrine of the Gospel-High-Priest, and the perfect Work he wrought in taking away Sin, and bringing in everlasting Righteousness; let us therefore persevere in the Faith and Hope of him, really, actually, stedfastly, retaining with all our Might and Power, whatsoever Insinuations may be used to entice us, or Vio<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lence by Persecutions, to force us from it, retaining still in Mind, Will, Affection and Operation.</ns0:note> hold fast the profession of <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">An <ns0:hi>outward Exhi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bition</ns0:hi> to the World both in Word and Deed, as we have it sincerely in our Hearts, solemnly owning in the Ordinances of God in his Church of <ns0:hi>the Hope</ns0:hi> we have in Christ our High-Priest, and of all that he hath purchased for us, and promised to perform in us, and to us, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 3.1, 6. and 4.14. and 6.11. <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 10.9, 10. 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 1.3, 21.</ns0:note> our faith without <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">

               <ns0:p n="24">24 And let us <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Having urged from the Gospel-Doctrine of our High-Priest, our Duty to God, the Spirit proceeds to shew what Influence it should have on Christians for performing their Duty one to another, in their Inspection and Observation of the whole Body of Christ, consisting of <ns0:hi>Iew</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Gentile,</ns0:hi> who have equally shared in Christ's Sacrifice, and are interested in, and related to his Person; and by the apprehensive and judicial Faculty so to discern the spiritual State and Con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dition of each other, and the whole, as every particular Member of it may be capable to animadvert, exhort, re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />prove, counsel or comfort, and act suitably and seasonably in the discharge of their mutual Duty, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 14.19. and 15.7, 14. <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 3.13. <ns0:hi>Colos.</ns0:hi> 3.16. 1 <ns0:hi>Thess.</ns0:hi> 5.11, 15.</ns0:note> consider one another, to pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />voke <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">

Chap. 6.4.</ns0:note> if we sin wilfully <ns0:hi>s</ns0:hi> after <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">2 Pet. 2.20, 21.</ns0:note> that we have received <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">After all this, to renounce the Profession of it, and to forsake the Assemblies where it is held forth; this is the spontaneous and wilful sinning: See <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 6.6.</ns0:note> the knowledg of the truth, there remaineth no more <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">This is unpardonable by the just Constitution of God in the Gospel, because no sacrifice can atone God for them; without which they cannot be pardoned, and the Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crifice of Christ, which could only do it, they renounce and desert; and so this, nor any other they can bring, can pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cure Pardon for them, so that their Sins remain in Guilt and Power on them, and between them and God's Wrath are they like irrecoverably to be ground to Perdition.</ns0:note> sacrifice for sins.</ns0:p>

               <ns0:p n="28">28 He <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">The Punishment threatned on such Sinners, is illustrated by an Instance proper to the <ns0:hi>Hebrews</ns0:hi>; for if the lesser Sin against <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi>'s Law was punished by Death, the greater Sin against the Gospel of Christ shall be more punished.                <ns0:p n="29">29 Of how much <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">The Expostulation aggravates both the Sin and the Pu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nishment in the Consequent on the former Assertion; a Punishment heavier, bitterer, sorer, more grievous, and unexpressibly greater than Death.</ns0:note> sorer punishment, sup<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pose ye, <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">You your selves being Judges, to whom I appeal about it; what can you suppose, think, or determine of it?</ns0:note>, shall he be thought <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Doth he fully deserve, and is liable to, by the Judgment of Man, but much more by the righteous and inexorable Judgment of God.</ns0:note> worthy, who hath <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Who sin<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />neth at an higher rate than a <ns0:hi>Iew</ns0:hi> against <ns0:hi>Moses</ns0:hi>'s Law, being an Apostate from the Gospel, a Revolter from, and a Rebel against it, discovering it by as much as in him lieth, tearing from his Throne God the Son incarnate, and tread<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing him under his Feet, wickedly undervaluing, and hor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ribly vilifying him, treating him with the greatest Contempt that can be expressed by such an action, as if he were the vilest Malefactor.                <ns0:p n="30">30 For <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>For,</ns0:hi> brings in the Proof of the Soreness of God's Pu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nishment to be afflicted on Apostates, from God's own Te<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stimony about it; which <ns0:hi>we</ns0:hi> who are conversant with the Scriptures, are well acquainted with, <ns0:hi>we know,</ns0:hi> what God hath spoken, and by whom he hath spoken it, <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 9.29.                      <ns0:hi>To me is Vengeance and Recompence</ns0:hi>; which are the words of the Hebrew Text. <ns0:hi>To me,</ns0:hi> the Soveraign Being, the Su<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />preme and Universal Law-giver and Judge, doth belong the Universal Right and Power of vindictive Justice. He is not only just and powerful, but actually manifesting both in his Retribution on them, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 32.41, 43. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 94.1. <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 12.19. 2 <ns0:hi>Thess.</ns0:hi> 1.8.</ns0:note> Ven<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />geance <ns0:hi>belongeth</ns0:hi> unto me, I will recompence, saith the Lord <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Iehovah</ns0:hi> saith it, who is faithful and true, powerful and constant to his Threatnings, as well as his Promises. The Soveraign Being of Righteousness, the same <ns0:hi>Iehovah</ns0:hi> as before, will rule, justifie, save, deliver, and vindicate his Covenant-People from the Contempt and vilifying of his Son and them, by punishing severely such, who by their Apostacy from him and them, are guilty of it. He will certainly take Vengeance on them, and thereby clear the Innocency, Truth and Goodness of his, who are trampled on by them.</ns0:note>

               <ns0:p n="35">35 Cast not away <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">This introduceth the last Direction for helping on their Perseverance in Christianity. <ns0:gap reason="foreign">

                     </ns0:gap> denieth all degrees of Apostacy, from secret undervaluing to an utter renouncing, not to slight, despise, or reject; they had endured already so much as might steel and fortifie them against what remained, and implieth the bold, resolute, and couragious Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tention, <ns0:hi>Ephes.</ns0:hi> 6.10, 16. of the Boldness of their Confession of the Christian Faith.                <ns0:p n="37">37 For <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">The Reason of their retaining their Confidence to the end, is the shortness of his coming, who will reward them for it, proved out of God's Promise written to, and for the Church, by <ns0:hi>Habakkuk, ch.</ns0:hi> 2.3.                <ns0:p n="38">38 Now <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">These are as the former, the Words of the Prophet <ns0:hi>Ha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bakkuk ch.</ns0:hi> 2.4. inforcing the former Duty pressed from the Gain of Perseverance, and the loss by withdrawing, when Christ shall come.
